configs.description: The chassis with two AC supplies and two fan modules fitted, front-to-rear air, before any part number: the shape every build below starts from.
configs.name: base

configs.description: Two DC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-511-DC-RED supplies and FAN-7011M-F fan modules. The data sheet lists no DC part number for the switch; the supplies are spares, and a DC build is ordered through the "#" configurable SKU.
configs.name: dc-f

configs.description: Two DC supplies and rear-to-front air: PWR-511-DC-BLUE supplies and FAN-7011M-R fan modules. No DC part number is listed for the switch.
configs.name: dc-r

configs.description: The 7280TR3-40C6 with two AC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-511-AC-RED supplies and FAN-7011M-F fan modules, all with red handles. Ordered as DCS-7280TR3-40C6-F.
configs.name: f

configs.description: The 7280TR3-40C6 with two AC supplies and rear-to-front air: PWR-511-AC-BLUE supplies and FAN-7011M-R fan modules, all with blue handles. Ordered as DCS-7280TR3-40C6-R.
configs.name: r

gaps.note: The data sheet gives 4 jacks of 10G only and 36 of 1G or 10G and says nowhere which four. All forty are modelled at 10G.
gaps.wanted: the guide's table of port groups for the TR3-40C6.

gaps.note: The photograph is too small to resolve any per-port lamp, so none is modelled and the port lamp states of guide Appendix A.1.2 are not attached to a port.

Which of the two RJ-45 jacks is the management port and which the console is read from the 7280CR3-36S figure of the same guide; the photograph shows two jacks and a USB port.

chassis.note: Guide Table 1: 48.3 x 4.4 x 46.9 cm (19 x 1.75 x 18.5 in), 9.6 kg (21.1 lbs). Data sheet: 43.99 x 4.37 x 46.9 cm (17.3 x 1.72 x 18.46 in), 21.1 lbs (9.57 kg). The width: 48.3 cm is over the mounting ears, so the body between them, which is what is modelled, is the data sheet's 43.99 cm (440.0 here), a 21.5 mm ear each side. The height is the data sheet's 43.7. The depth is the data sheet's 469.0 (the guide's 46.9 cm). The weights agree (9.6 kg rounds 9.57 kg); no size conflict. 1RU.

colour.note: The front plate is a dark slate: the median of bare-plate pixels at the right of the photograph reads RGB (107, 109, 118), taken as #6e7178. The photograph's lighting is not known, so the shade is estimated; the other 7280R3 models in the library are #aaabad.

configurations.note: Data sheet ordering information: DCS-7280TR3-40C6-F and -R ("40x10GbE RJ45 and 6x100G QSFP switch router, front to rear air, 2 x AC" and "rear to front air, 2 x AC"). The data sheet lists no K, M or A form of the TR3-40C6. The "#" SKU ("configurable fans and psu") is an order of parts, not a part number a DCIM can hold, and is not listed. The data sheet lists no DC build of the switch: the PWR-511-DC-RED and -BLUE supplies are spares, so the DC configurations are examples with no part number. There is no empty-bay (-S) configuration: no -S suffix exists in this family and the guide draws no blank for a power supply or fan module. The DCS-7280SR3E-40YC6-M, the other model of this slice, shares the 7280SR3-40YC6's face and is already a configuration of arista/7280sr3-40yc6.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's Chapter 3 mounts the switch with the accessory-kit brackets and shows them in isometric drawings of a different switch that carry no measure. The data sheet lists the spares KIT-7101, KIT-2POST-1U-NT, KIT-7101-RK, KIT-7101-LD-RK and KIT-GND-EXT-1RU. No figure measures a bracket position, and the kit guides are not held, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits. Recorded in the gap rack-ears.

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, altitude 0 to 3,000 m, humidity 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. Data sheet: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -40 to 70 C, humidity 5 to 95 percent, altitude 0 to 3,000 m. Storage temperature and humidity differ: gap `environment`, the guide's used.

front-legend.note: The photograph shows model print in small type under the maker's wordmark at the top left. THE WORDMARK IS NOT DRAWN: a logo-zone region is reserved over it and the plain model text is set, as the data sheet names the model.

front-ports.note: Data sheet photograph at 0.895 px/mm. Forty RJ-45 jacks in two stacked rows, twenty columns in five blocks of four (ports 1 to 40): the first jack of each block reads 19, 77, 135.5, 194 and 252 px across, which is 20.1, 84.9, 150.2, 215.6 and 280.4 mm, a block step of 64.9 mm; inside a block the jacks step 13.97 mm (the registry's ganged-jack pitch, which the photograph reads at 13.9). Six QSFP100 cages in two stacked rows of three columns (41 to 46), centred 313, 336 and 359.5 px across = 348.5, 374.2 and 400.3 mm, a pitch of 25.9 (the cages sit in a wider bezel than the registry's 18.5 mm opening). The jack rows read centred 14.6 and 29.1 mm down, a row pitch of 14.5, and the QSFP rows 14.75 and 28.95 mm down, 14.2. The upper jack is the registry's mirror of the lower (turned 180), as the Catalyst 4948E draws its stacked jacks; the QSFP rows are belly to belly, upper upright and lower turned 180, the library's convention, which the photograph is too small to confirm.

fru-bays.note: Guide Appendix E (E.2 power supplies, E.3 fan modules) gives removal and installation procedures, and the data sheet calls the supplies "1+1 hot-swappable" and the fans "hot-swap". SO THE TWO POWER SUPPLIES AND THE TWO FAN MODULES ARE BAYS. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit. The management block, the USB port and the console port are part of the chassis and are placements.

gate-1-front.note: THE FRONT IS PHOTO-MEASURED. The data sheet's photograph of the 7280TR3-40C6 (page 5, first row of the model table) is a near-straight-on image stored at 396 x 39 px. The chassis fills it: 394 px between the edges of the face (x = 1 to 395) against the 440.0 mm body gives 0.895 px/mm across, and 39 px against the 43.7 mm height gives 0.892 px/mm down, so the two axes agree to 0.4 percent and the face is taken as orthographic. One pixel is 1.12 mm, so every position is good to about 1 mm and none is better, and every one is `estimated` because it is read off a photograph and no dimension states it. How: the scale anchor is the 440.0 mm body (the data sheet's 43.99 cm) and the 43.7 mm height; positions were read from dark-run scans of the photograph along rows 15 and 23 (the jack openings) and down columns through a jack, a QSFP cage and the management stack, the counts from a five-times enlargement. The RJ-45 pitch inside a block reads 12.5 px = 13.9 mm, which is the registry's 13.97 for a ganged jack, on a quantity the scale never saw.

gate-1-rear.note: Figure D-1 is a 553 x 141 px raster whose chassis is 551 px between its edges and 54 px tall (aspect 10.2 against 10.07), 1.252 px/mm over the 440 mm body; positions are good to about 0.8 mm. The guide draws the rear generically (D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. The 7280TR3-40C6 is mapped to D-1 by its two fan modules (data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 2 (N+1 redundant)"), its 1RU height and its two power supplies. D-1 draws a management block between the left supply and the first fan; the photograph of this model carries the management ports at the front, so that block is NOT drawn here and the space is plain metal (gap `rear-mgmt-position`). THE MAPPING IS ESTIMATED.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. EOS names ports Ethernet1 to Ethernet46 and Management1; this is the vendor's convention and no held document prints it.

lifecycle.note: Searched 2026-10-24 in the held documents (guide, data sheet) for an end-of-sale or end-of-life notice for the 7280TR3-40C6: none. The sources the 7280SR3-40YC6 records (web searches of Arista's end-of-sale notices, 2026-10-23) returned notices for older 7280 models and for the 7280SR3K-48YC8 and 7280CR3K-36S series, not for this one.

management-block.note: The photograph shows a stack of RJ-45, USB and RJ-45 at the right, 372 to 386 px = 414 to 430 mm across and 5 to 36 mm down. It is read as the Ethernet management port (top), the USB port and the RJ-45 console port, the order of Figure C-5 of the same guide (the 7280CR3-36S, whose management block is also at the front); the photograph cannot say which RJ-45 is which. Plate and cutouts are the 7280CR3-36S's, moved to the measured x.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat. The guide's installation figures are isometric. Each carries an `empty` sentence. The 1RU grounding point is on the bottom of the chassis (guide section 4.2, Table 5, KIT-GND-EXT-1RU); no figure measures it.

port-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.2 gives the port lamp states of the family, but the photograph at 0.9 px/mm shows no per-port lamp that can be placed or counted (row 35 of the photograph carries a line of tiny marks under the jacks and the cages, unresolved). No port lamp is modelled (gap `port-lamps`).

port-numbering.note: The photograph's numerals are not legible and no held document lists them, so no numeral is printed. Ids follow the 7280SR3-40YC6's precedent of the same guide (Figure C-7 prints 1 over 2 up to 46): the jacks are 1 to 40 and the QSFP cages 41 to 46, the odd number the upper cage. The numbering is estimated. EOS interface names are not printed on the metal and are not modelled.

port-speeds.note: Data sheet model comparison: "10G Only RJ45 Ports 4" and "1G/10G RJ45 Ports 36". No document says which four jacks are 10G only, so all forty are modelled at the highest native rate, 10G, and the split is in attrs and in gap `rj45-speeds`.

power.note: Guide Table 4: typical / maximum 186 W / 242 W for the 7280TR3-40C6 with PWR-511-AC or PWR-511-DC. The data sheet states the same figures with typical "measured at 25C ambient with 50% load on all ports".

rear.note: Figure D-1 at 1.252 px/mm, the rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing. PS1 is the left and PS2 the right (callouts 1 and 6). Each power supply module is 73.5 mm wide (the data sheet's "73.5MM") at 4.4 and 361.5 mm across and 1.85 mm down. Two fan modules 78.6 mm wide at 105.7 and 276.6 mm across and 2.55 mm down, the positions the 7280SR3-40YC6 reads from the same figure. Between the fans is a grey plate printed with ASSY NUMBER, SERIAL NUMBER and MAC ADDRESS fields and, under them, PS1 and PS2 legends beside airflow arrows (the arrows are not drawn).

rear-fan.note: Data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 2 (N+1 redundant)", "Fan Tray FAN-7011M" and the spares FAN-7011M-F (front-to-rear) and FAN-7011M-R (rear-to-front). Guide section 2.1: a red handle is an air-exit module and a blue handle an air-inlet one, and every module must have the same direction. The two fan modules are bays that accept FAN-7011M-F or -R; the -R configurations seat the blue modules. The components are the ones the 7280SR3-40YC6 seats.

sources.note: 7280R3 Series Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, document DOC-07041-01, 63 pages, PDF created 2025-05-16 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280R3.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage), Table 3 (power input), Table 4 (power draw and supported supplies), section 2.1 (airflow orientation, handle colour), Table 5 (grounding), Appendix A (status indicators, Tables 9 to 13), Appendix D (Figure D-1, the rear panel with two fan modules), Appendix E (field replacement). 7280R3 Series Data Center Switch Router Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 03-0045-59, dated August 11th, 2025 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7280R3-Data-Sheet.pdf): the model comparison of the 7280TR3-40C6, the power supply specifications, the ordering information and, on page 5, the photograph of the face that is the only front source. The guide lists the DCS-7280TR3-40C6 in its scope, Table 1 and Table 4 but has NO FRONT FIGURE for it: Appendix C draws C-1 to C-8 for the other models and none is captioned for this one. The 2022 7280 1RU Gen 3 guide (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280_1RU_Gen3.pdf) does not list this model. Held and checked first: intake COVERAGE.md and SOURCES.md, which list no photograph other than the data sheet's, no Visio stencil, 3D model or CAD file for this model (Arista publishes none; the stencil zip could not be fetched). No drawing, photograph or logo is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

speed-tag.note: A small cyan tag sits above the management block, 372 to 381 px = 414 to 424 mm across and 2.2 to 4.5 mm down. It is drawn in its colour and extent; what it reads is not legible.

status-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.1, Table 9: a system status lamp, a fan status lamp and a status lamp for each of the two power supplies. The photograph shows four small marks in a column at the top right, x about 390 px = 434.5 mm and 3 to 11 mm down; four lamps are placed at 4.0, 6.6, 9.2 and 11.8 mm in the guide's order of its other models (system, fan, PS1, PS2). Their order and glyphs are not legible in the photograph and no legend is drawn (gap `front-legends`).

vents.note: The photograph shows a perforated row along the top (rows 3 to 6, x 26 to 365 px = 28 to 407 mm) and a row of slits along the bottom lip (rows 34 to 37, x 12 to 290 px). Each is drawn in its measured extent, not hole by hole.
